main_turf.bias_notes: Left-handed, completely flat galloping track. Features a straight mile course for all races from 5f up to 1m, and a round course featuring two sharp, tight bends. The straight rides exceptionally long, making it difficult for lone front-runners to wire fields unless they dictate a soft pace. Rewards patient, well-timed challenges.
main_turf.post_bias: On the straight course (5f to 1m), draw bias is heavily dictated by where the field races. If runners split toward the far rail, low numbers hold a slight ground-saving edge; if they race down the stands' side, high draws can come into play. On the round course, inside barriers (stalls 1-4) are crucial to avoid losing ground around the sharp bends.

handicapping_angles.long_straight_patience_factor: Because Redcar's straight is flat and long, horses that hit the front too soon often get collared. Upgrade strong-finishing pressers ('P') and stalkers over relentless, un-rateable front-runners ('E').
handicapping_angles.northern_stable_targeting: Prominent northern yards (e.g., Tim Easterby, Richard Fahey) frequently target Redcar lower-tier handicaps. Pay close attention to stable placement and market confidence from these yards.
handicapping_angles.straight_course_ground_bias: In large-field straight handicaps (5f/6f), check the going description. On good-to-firm ground, horses racing near the center or tracking the stands' side often find the freshest paths.
handicapping_angles.round_course_sharp_bend_penalty: In round course races (1m2f+), horses caught wide around the tight bottom bend leak valuable ground. Upgrade rail-skimmers and handy types over deep closers.
